Nine Collages: The New Graphics by Weingart

Weingart’s poster and order form for his own series of nine hand-printed collages, laid out as a sheet of framed panels around one large collage.

Source
Letterform Archive: Legacies of Swiss Style, Part 2—Wolfgang Weingart
Creator
Wolfgang Weingart
Made
1974–1975 (Letterform Archive)
Style
New Wave typography (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Kinetic, rebellious, layered, experimental
Evidence
Inspected Letterform Archive’s photograph of the Archive’s copy (2496 × 3000) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Letterform Archive says the Nine Collages series came from darkroom experiments of the 1960s and early 1970s with “hand-cut films, barely-legible type, and the deliberate overlap of halftones to produce moiré effects”. Letterform Archive.

The poster text offers the collages, 59 × 49 cm, for sale by post from Basel, and its biography says Weingart taught typography at the School of Design in Basel from 1968.

Observed

  • The title is set in heavy grotesque capitals across the top: “NINE COLLAGES: THE NEW GRAPHICS BY WEINGART”.
  • Thin rules divide the sheet into panels of different sizes. Each small panel shows one collage and a bold caption such as “COLLAGE 5/1974”.
  • Collage 6 is made of spaced letters and dots (“1 8 9-1”, “E”, “T”, “H”) scattered on white. Collage 5 has a stepped line, a small grid, arcs, and “STO?”.
  • The large central collage is a black flame-like shape that holds halftone photographs of a cemetery, a garden, and a woman, with black dots, short rays, and a white cross.
  • The sale text uses bold capitals with a much larger price. The order form at right is set vertically, with “Order Form” in large type.
  • The biography at the bottom left is set in a typewriter face.

Why it belongs

The poster shows that the style can use a plain framed grid as a container, as long as what happens inside the frames breaks it.

The typewriter biography is one of the few monospaced passages in Weingart’s work here; it is a small caption, not the main voice.

Borrow

Frame small experiments in a grid of thin rules, with one bold caption under each.

Set a form or call to action vertically along one edge.

Scatter a few spaced letters and dots in open white space as a quiet panel next to dense ones.
